title: Suspension Bridge Stress Test with Vehicle Loading
prompt:
Create a single-HTML-file Three.js application simulating a suspension bridge with spring-mass cable physics, stress visualization, and a vehicle driving across it.

【Three.js Import (must follow exactly)】
Place in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

【Scene Setup】
- Background: overcast sky gradient (#B0C4DE to #F0F0F0)
- Camera: perspective, starting at (0, 15, 40) looking at (0, 0, 0)
- Lights: directional (casts shadows), hemisphere light (sky blue / ground brown)
- Water plane below the bridge at y=-5, using a semi-transparent blue plane
- Two tower structures (pylons) at x=-20 and x=+20, each a pair of tall boxes (1x30x1) with a crossbar at top
- OrbitControls with damping

【Bridge Physics Model: Spring-Mass System】
The bridge deck is modeled as a chain of N=40 mass nodes connected by springs:
- Nodes evenly spaced from x=-20 to x=+20 (1.0m apart)
- Each node has mass m=0.5 kg, position (x, y, z), velocity (vx, vy, vz)
- Structural springs connect adjacent deck nodes: stiffness k_deck = 500 N/m, rest length = 1.0m
- Gravity g = 9.81 m/s^2 acts on all nodes
- The first and last nodes are pinned (anchored to the towers)

Main suspension cables (catenary):
- Two main cables (one on each side, z = -1.5 and z = +1.5) run from tower top to tower top
- Each cable has 40 nodes matching deck positions
- Cable nodes connected by springs: k_cable = 1000 N/m
- Cable endpoints are pinned to tower tops

Vertical hangers:
- Vertical springs connect each cable node to the corresponding deck node
- Hanger stiffness: k_hanger = 200 N/m, rest length = proportional to catenary sag at that point
- Hangers only pull (tension only, no compression): if hanger would compress, force = 0

Damping: velocity damping factor 0.995 per step (multiply velocity by 0.995 each step)

Integration: Verlet or semi-implicit Euler, dt=0.005s, multiple substeps per frame.

【Deck Visualization】
Render deck segments as flat boxes between consecutive nodes. Color each segment based on stress:
- Stress = |actual_length - rest_length| / rest_length (strain)
- Color mapping: green (strain < 0.02) -> yellow (0.02-0.05) -> orange (0.05-0.1) -> red (strain > 0.1)
- Use MeshStandardMaterial with color updated each frame

【Cable Visualization】
Render cables as thick lines (THREE.Line or tube geometry). Cable color: dark gray (#333333).
Render hangers as thin lines from cable to deck.

【Vehicle (CesiumMilkTruck.glb)】
Load CesiumMilkTruck.glb as the vehicle:
- Scale to fit approximately 3 units long
- Vehicle drives across the bridge from left (x=-20) to right (x=+20)
- Vehicle speed controlled by slider (default 2 m/s)
- Vehicle applies a downward load to the nearest deck nodes (distribute load to 2-3 nearest nodes using inverse-distance weighting)
- Vehicle load force: vehicleMass * g, where vehicleMass = 5.0 kg (scaled for visual effect)
- Vehicle y-position tracks the deck surface at its current x-position (interpolate between node heights)
- When vehicle reaches the end, it wraps back to the start

【Wind Effect】
Lateral wind force applied to all deck and cable nodes:
  windForce.z = windStrength * sin(time * 0.3 + nodeIndex * 0.2)
This creates a wave-like lateral sway pattern.

【Controls】
(1) Vehicle speed slider (id='slider-speed'): range 0 to 5, step 0.1, default 2
(2) Vehicle mass slider (id='slider-mass'): range 1 to 20, step 0.5, default 5
(3) Wind strength slider (id='slider-wind'): range 0 to 3, step 0.1, default 0
(4) Keyboard: 'Space' to pause/resume, 'R' to reset bridge to equilibrium, 'V' to toggle vehicle visibility

【HUD (id='hud')】
Semi-transparent panel at top-left:
- id='hud-vehicle-x': Vehicle X position (1 decimal)
- id='hud-max-stress': Maximum deck stress ratio (3 decimals)
- id='hud-max-deflection': Maximum vertical deflection from rest (2 decimals)
- id='hud-cable-tension': Average cable tension in N (1 decimal)
- id='hud-wind': Current wind strength (1 decimal)
- id='hud-sim-time': Simulation time (1 decimal)

【State Management】
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
{
  frameCount: number,
  vehicleX: number,             // vehicle position along bridge
  vehicleSpeed: number,         // current speed setting
  vehicleMass: number,          // current mass setting
  maxStress: number,            // highest strain ratio on any deck segment
  maxDeflection: number,        // largest vertical drop from rest position (positive = downward)
  avgCableTension: number,      // average tension in cable springs
  windStrength: number,         // current wind setting
  deckNodeCount: number,        // number of deck nodes
  midDeckY: number,             // y-position of the middle deck node
  isPaused: boolean,
  simTime: number
}

【Physics Constraints】
- Bridge should sag under vehicle weight, with deflection proportional to load
- Maximum deflection should occur near the vehicle position
- Cable tension should increase when bridge is loaded
- Lateral sway from wind should be visible but not cause instability
- After vehicle passes, bridge should return close to its unloaded shape (within damping time)

Output a single HTML file.
physics_constraints: Spring-mass system for deck (40 nodes, k_deck=500 N/m) and cables (k_cable=1000 N/m). Verlet/semi-implicit Euler dt=0.005s. Vehicle load distributed to nearest nodes. Stress coloring based on strain. Tension-only hangers. Velocity damping 0.995. Bridge deflection proportional to vehicle mass.
difficulty_analysis: L5: (1) Complex spring-mass network with deck, cables, and hanger subsystems; (2) Catenary cable initialization geometry; (3) Stress-based color mapping updated per frame; (4) Vehicle load distribution with inverse-distance weighting; (5) Vehicle y-tracking by interpolating deck node heights; (6) Tension-only hanger constraint; (7) Wind wave pattern across bridge; (8) GLB model driving across dynamic surface.
